Landing.privacyLead: Not just a promise in the footer: Encore was built to work without holding on to your data.

Privacy.title: Privacy
Privacy.lead: Encore was built to use as little of your data as possible, and almost everything happens on your own device. Here you can see what we use, where it's kept, for how long and how to cancel access whenever you like.
summary: The history you add is read on your device and isn't sent to us or anyone else.
No sign-up, we don't keep your music, and we don't use tools that track your visits.
In Connect mode, what comes from Spotify stays in this tab only, and your Spotify connection is saved on this device, protected so only Encore can read it.

what.title: What data we use
what.uploadTitle: Upload mode: the file you add
what.upload: From your history we only read: the day and time each song played, how long it played, the song, artist and album names, the song's Spotify code, where you listened (phone, computer…) and whether you skipped it or played it on shuffle.
what.uploadDiscarded: Your internet address (IP), the country you were connected from and everything else in the file are set aside while reading and never used.
what.connect: With your permission, we see your basic profile (account code, name and photo), your tops, what you played recently and your liked songs. Encore only asks to see: it can't change anything in your account.
what.demo: Uses only made-up data, created on your device. No personal data is used.

where.title: Where the data lives
where.body: Your file is read on the device itself, inside this page. In Connect mode, Encore fetches the information from Spotify for you and hands back only what the screen needs, keeping nothing along the way. The site is hosted by Vercel, a website hosting company, and in Connect mode those requests go through Vercel's and Spotify's systems, which may be outside Brazil. This transfer to another country is needed to give you what you asked for (LGPD, art. 33, IX).

howLong.title: For how long
items: Added history: only in this tab's memory, until you reload or close the page.
What comes from Spotify (Connect mode): stays in this browser tab only, for at most 12 hours, and is deleted when you click Log out.
Your Spotify connection (Connect mode): saved in this browser in a protected cookie, lasts at most 30 days and is deleted when you click Log out.

Running records: Encore only notes which part of the site was used, whether it worked and how long it took, with nothing about your music or your account. Vercel, which hosts the site, also notes details of each visit (such as your internet address, the IP, and the page opened) and keeps them for a short time (about 1 hour on the plan in use), under its own privacy policy.

legal.title: Why we're allowed to use this data
legal.body: We only use this data to give you what you asked for: your stats (the legal basis in Brazil's LGPD, art. 7, V). In Connect mode, we also rely on the permission you give on Spotify, which you can take back at any time. We don't use your data for ads or to build a profile of you, and we don't hand it to other companies for their own use.

sharing.title: Sharing
sharing.body: We don't sell or share your data. Spotify is where Connect mode data comes from, and Vercel is the company that hosts the site. Cards you make stay on your device until you choose to share them.

rights.title: Your rights and how to cancel access
items: Delete the history you added: close or reload the tab.
Leave Connect mode: click Log out. That deletes your saved connection and what came from Spotify in this tab.

Under the LGPD (art. 18), you can ask us to confirm whether we use your data, see it, correct it, take it to another service, delete it and learn who it was shared with. Since we don't keep your data, there's no copy of ours to look up or export. You can still make any request through the contact above.
You can also complain to Brazil's National Data Protection Authority (ANPD), the government body that enforces the LGPD.
Remove Encore's access to your Spotify account: remove the app at

cookies.title: Cookies
cookies.body: Cookies are small files a website saves in your browser. Encore only uses essential ones: one that keeps you connected in Connect mode, and a temporary 10-minute one while you log in with Spotify. Your language preference may also be saved in your browser.

Onboarding.title: Request your history from Spotify
Onboarding.lead: Encore uses your full history, which Spotify emails you when you ask for it. It's free and covers everything since you created your account.
Onboarding.wait: Spotify can take up to 30 days to send it. It usually arrives sooner.

open.title: Open your Spotify account privacy page
open.body: Sign in and scroll down to "Download your data".

select.title: Tick the extended streaming history
select.bodyAfter: and untick the rest. That's your full history, and it's all we need.

confirm.title: Confirm through the email Spotify sends you
confirm.body: The request only starts after you click the confirmation link.

return.title: When the file arrives, come back here
return.body: Add the file on the upload page just as it came, without unzipping it.

UNSUPPORTED_FILE.title: This file won't work
UNSUPPORTED_FILE.body: "{file}" doesn't look like the Spotify file. Add the file from Spotify's email (its name ends in .zip).

INVALID_ZIP.title: We couldn't open this file
INVALID_ZIP.body: "{file}" seems to be damaged or isn't the Spotify file. Download it again from the link in the email and add it without unzipping.

UNSAFE_PATH.title: Something's off with this file
UNSAFE_PATH.body: We found something inside it that the Spotify file doesn't have, so we stopped to be safe. Download the file again from the link in Spotify's email.

TOO_MANY_ENTRIES.title: This file isn't what we expected
TOO_MANY_ENTRIES.body: It has more than {limit} files inside, and Spotify's usually has far fewer. Check that it's the right file.

ENTRY_TOO_LARGE.title: File too big
ENTRY_TOO_LARGE.body: "{entry}" is over {limit} MB once opened. To be safe, we don't read files that big.

TOTAL_TOO_LARGE.title: File too big
TOTAL_TOO_LARGE.body: To be safe, we only read histories up to {limit} MB once opened, and this one is over the limit.

COMPRESSION_RATIO.title: This file isn't what we expected
COMPRESSION_RATIO.body: "{entry}" grows more than {limit} times when opened, far more than a normal history. To be safe, we stopped reading.

NO_HISTORY_FILES.title: This file doesn't have your full history
NO_HISTORY_FILES.body: We couldn't find your songs in it. Check that you asked Spotify for the "Extended streaming history".

WRONG_EXPORT.title: This is the "Account data" package
WRONG_EXPORT.body: It only covers the last year, with fewer details. Ask for the "Extended streaming history" to see everything.

INVALID_JSON.title: Part of the file is damaged
INVALID_JSON.body: We couldn't read "{entry}". Download the file again from the link in Spotify's email.

UNEXPECTED_FORMAT.title: We don't recognise this file
UNEXPECTED_FORMAT.body: "{entry}" doesn't have what a Spotify history usually has. It may be a different file, or Spotify changed the format.

INVALID_RECORDS.title: Part of the history can't be read
INVALID_RECORDS.body: More than 5% of the songs in "{entry}" ({invalid} of {total}) came in a format we don't recognise. The file may be damaged, or Spotify changed the format.

INTERNAL.title: Your device couldn't cope
INTERNAL.body: Something went wrong while reading the file, maybe low memory. Close other tabs and try again, or use a computer.

OFFLINE.title: No internet
OFFLINE.body: Looks like you're offline. Connect and try again: your file still stays on your device.
